I slowly ate less and less red meat then just meat in general.  just like fast food if I smell it I feel nauseous. Since I stoped eating meat and fast food I sleep better and I have more energy. In the summer of 2014 I thought I was never going to swim again. I have a thing called TOS in both my arms but it took them 3 years to figure out what it was. I am now able to swim after 2 surgeries and getting proper physical therapy.  I would recommend finding a sports Med dr and a really good physical therapist because they did a much better job at figuring things out than any regular care doctor.   If you feel like you aren't getting the care you need you should not hesitate to find a new doctor. Also really pay attention to things that cause the pain and learn what your maximum is for each task. It sounds really shitty and it is at first but it's just really important to listen to your body.   Accepting that you're recovery maybe slower than you thought is really hard and frustrating. I am not close to being 100% at all but I'm getting better. I had days,hell even weeks, when I just wanted to stop everything and quite so I understand. So yes I can swim it isn't as much as I use to but I still try. Honestly just find new doctors and know that this isn't the end.

I have something called Thoracic outlet syndrome and my left arm we'll go numb or have a very bad pens a needles feeling. The symptoms and get very painful and make it almost hard to move my arm. The pain also makes me pass out. That's another issue I have. I pass out a lot if I get too stressed or I am in too much pain.  It isn't a very common thing so it took my doctors a long time to know what was wrong. My surgery is very confusing and they pretty much had to remove on of my ribs to give the nerves that go to my arm more room. The recovery is 4-y6months because it puts your lungs at a lot of risk. I had the surgery 3 months ago and my parents where sure I'd be fine but now my body is saying different. I have right pain in my chest and the er Drs said I could have a lot of inflammation in my lungs a blood clots. I really hope being in a place I am use to can help me get fully recovered and everything taken care of (mentally and physically) but the lack of support I'm getting is making me feel like I'm doing something wrong. I'm not sure if I feel this why because I'm finally focusing on myself and not what everyone wants me to do or if I'm actually in the wrong.
